preventative-maintenance.metaTitle: Preventative Maintenance — Elite Sports Floor Care
preventative-maintenance.metaDescription: A programmed annual maintenance cycle that keeps your timber sports floor's coating ahead of the wear, with a written report and forward plan every visit.

hero.alt: Technician with a clipboard beside a school hall court
hero.title: Preventative Maintenance
hero.lead: One scheduled visit a year, booked in advance, that keeps the coating ahead of the wear — so nothing ever becomes urgent.

involves.title: The cheapest work is the work you plan
paragraphs: Most of the floors we're called to rescue didn't fail suddenly — they just went a few too many years without anyone looking. A maintenance program takes that off your plate: we set the schedule, we turn up, and you get a short report telling you what the floor needs next and when.

Because we're planning years ahead instead of reacting, the work lands in your quiet weeks — term breaks, off-season, shutdown periods — and the cost sits in your budget as one predictable line item instead of an unwelcome capital request.
Turnaround: the annual inspection and clean is usually a single day or evening, with no court closure beyond that shift.

recoating.metaTitle: Sports Floor Recoating — Elite Sports Floor Care
recoating.metaDescription: Screen and re-coat your timber sports floor in sports-grade finish — ready to play the next morning. Serving schools, stadiums, gyms and rec centres across Victoria.

hero.alt: Coating machine laying finish across a timber court
hero.title: Sports Floor Recoating
hero.lead: A screen and re-coat renews the wear layer without touching the timber underneath — and you're playing on it the next morning.

involves.title: A new wear layer, not a new floor
paragraphs: Every timber sports floor wears from the top down. The coating takes the punishment — shoes, ball impact, drag marks, cleaning chemicals — and once it thins out, the timber starts taking it instead. That's when a floor ends up needing a full sand, and a floor can only be sanded a handful of times in its life.

Recoating gets in before that happens. We abrade the existing finish back to a key, clean it down to bare dust-free timber-safe surface, then lay fresh sports-grade coats. The floor comes back with even gloss, correct slip resistance and the ball response players expect.
Turnaround: a single court is typically a two-night job, and most floors are ready for use the next morning. We work nights, weekends and school holidays so nothing comes off your booking sheet.

items: Pre-coat moisture and adhesion test
Full floor abrasion (screen) of existing finish

Two coats of sports-grade finish to AS 3610 slip range

Post-job photo record and care sheet for your cleaners

depth.iframeTitle: Interactive comparison of a court floor's recoat versus full-sand depth budget
depth.staticAlt: Floor screening machine abrading a timber court surface
depth.title: Why a recoat beats a re-sand
depth.body: Every court has a fixed depth budget. A recoat only renews the finish on top — do it as often as the schedule calls for and the board never gets any thinner. A full sand cuts into the timber itself, and there's only so much of it before you're into the tongue and groove. Try the model: recoat as many times as you like, then see how fast a floor runs out of safe sands.
legend: Current surface — what players are on today

deep-cleaning.metaTitle: Deep Cleaning — Elite Sports Floor Care
deep-cleaning.metaDescription: Sports-floor-safe machine deep cleaning that lifts embedded grime and rubber marking mopping leaves behind, with same-morning turnaround.

hero.alt: Rotary floor machine mid-clean on a timber court
hero.title: Deep Cleaning
hero.lead: Mopping moves the dirt around. A proper deep clean lifts the embedded grime and rubber that's dulling your floor and eating the coating.

involves.title: Grip you can feel, gloss you can see
paragraphs: Court shoes leave rubber behind. Add dust, sweat, spilled drinks and whatever the last cleaning product left on the surface, and you get a floor that looks tired, plays slippery in patches and grips oddly in others. Players notice it before anyone else does.

We use sports-floor-safe equipment and pH-correct chemistry — no water flooding, no aggressive strippers, nothing that will haze the coating or swell the boards. The residue comes off, the surface texture comes back, and the coating stops being sanded down by the grit sitting on top of it.
Turnaround: a single court is an overnight job and is ready for use the same morning. No dry-out period.

court-line-marking.metaTitle: Court Line Marking — Elite Sports Floor Care
court-line-marking.metaDescription: Court lines set out to current basketball, netball, badminton, volleyball and futsal dimensions, hand-masked and sealed under the floor coating.

hero.alt: Fresh court lines being masked and set out on timber
hero.title: Court Line Marking
hero.lead: Set out to the current governing-body dimensions, masked by hand and sealed under coating so the lines last as long as the finish.

involves.title: Lines that hold up to a referee's eye
paragraphs: Faded, doubled-up or out-of-code lines are the fastest way to lose a fixture. We re-set courts to the current dimensions for basketball, netball, badminton, volleyball and futsal — and where a hall carries four or five sports at once, we work out a colour and priority scheme that stays readable instead of turning into spaghetti.

Every line is set out from datum, masked by hand and rolled in sports-grade paint, then sealed under the floor coating. That's the part that matters: sealed lines wear at the same rate as the finish instead of lifting at the edges within a season.
Turnaround: usually done as part of a recoat — a full re-set on a single court is two to three nights including seal coats.

items: Set-out to current basketball, netball and badminton codes

Removal of redundant or superseded lines

Sealed under two coats of sports finish

hero.title: Floor Inspections
hero.lead: A free, no-obligation condition report: what your floor needs, what it doesn't, what it will cost and when. In writing, with photos.

involves.title: Know what you're sitting on
paragraphs: Most facility managers inherit their floor. Nobody hands over the coating history, so the first honest answer to "how long has it got?" usually comes from someone standing on it with a torch and a test kit. That's what this visit is.

We'll tell you plainly whether the floor is a recoat, a re-sand or fine as it is — including when the answer is "leave it another two years." You get a written report you can attach to a budget submission, and a costed recommendation with no obligation to book anything.
Turnaround: the visit takes about an hour per court and doesn't interrupt play. Report lands within three business days.
